comment: Coverage floors, checked by tests/coverage_merge.js --check (run by ./run-coverage.sh). Falling below any of these fails the run. Each is what a run achieved less a margin of 1 of a point, because a job skipped for want of a service takes its lines with it; --write-floors applies that margin. Raise them deliberately when coverage improves; never lower one without saying in the commit message what stopped being tested.
measured: A CLEAN RUN OF ONE TREE, and that is the whole of the 2026-09-10 change to this file. These are read on a GitHub runner that has never seen another run, and until that day ./run-coverage.sh kept a week of browser snapshots — so the frontend number was written from a local union of up to six runs and checked against one. 74.1 was never reached by any single run and could not be: the same tree measured 70.1 in CI and 72.3 on a developer's machine. The launcher empties coverage/frontend/.nyc_output now, so a local run and a CI run measure the same thing; the frontend numbers below are GitHub Actions run 34482736026's, which is the honest floor to start the ratchet from again. The other three are unchanged and were already per-run (c8 writes its temp directories fresh), which is why frontend was the one domain that disagreed.
